title: Linear Search on Strings: Finding a Name in a List
description: Search a list of names with strcmp, and see why == quietly fails on words.
congratsText: You can now search a list of names and say why strcmp is the only way to compare two words.
objectives: Explain what strcmp gives back and why the test is written == 0.
Predict the row number a name search reports, including -1.
Explain why == compares addresses instead of letters.
Apply the same search shape to a different list of words.
recap: strcmp gives back 0 when two words match, so the test is == 0.
A row number means found; -1 means no row matched, and case matters.
== compares two addresses, compiles without warning, and never matches.
searchCity reuses the shape unchanged — only the list and name differ.

chunks.text: searchName(char list[][20], int size, char target[]) keeps the same loop as a number search. The list is now a grid of rows, and the target is now a word.

check.question: What is searchName handed as its third thing?
options: The word it is looking for
The row it should start on

chunks.text: strcmp walks two words letter by letter and hands back 0 when it runs out of differences. So 0 means same, not true.

check.question: What does strcmp give back for two equal words?
options: 1, because the answer is true
0, because nothing differs

chunks.text: That is why the test is written if (strcmp(list[i], target) == 0). On a match it runs return i;; if the loop ends with no match, return -1; runs instead.

check.question: Why is == 0 written after the strcmp call?
options: Because 0 is the answer that means same
Because strcmp counts down toward zero

quiz.question: What number does found hold after this runs?
options: 0, because strcmp matched the word Cely
2, the row number where Cely sits
3, counting the rows from 1 instead of 0
4, the number of letters in the word Cely

chunks.text: searchName(names, 5, "Ana") hands back 0. Row 0 is a real row, so 0 here means found, at the front.

check.question: Does 0 mean the search failed?
options: No, it is the first row
Yes, nothing was found

chunks.text: searchName(names, 5, "Zeny") has to check all five rows. None match, so the loop ends and the function hands back -1 instead.

check.question: How many rows does the search for Zeny check?
options: One, then it gives up
All five, then it stops

chunks.text: strcmp is case sensitive. A capital A and a small a are different letters, so searchName(names, 5, "ana") hands back -1 even though Ana is in the list.

check.question: Why does searching for ana give -1?
options: The list holds Ana with a capital A
Short words are skipped by the loop

quiz.question: Type the number found holds after this runs.

chunks.text: A word in C is not held in one box. list[i] and target are each an address — a note saying where the letters are kept.

check.question: What does list[i] hold on its own?
options: Where the letters are kept
The letters themselves

chunks.text: Two words kept in two different places have two different addresses. So list[i] == target compares the two notes, not the letters, and stays false even when the words match.

check.question: What does list[i] == target actually compare?
options: The letters inside both words
The two addresses

chunks.text: The worst part: it compiles with no warning. Searching for Cely just reports -1 as if Cely were not in the list at all.

check.question: How does the compiler react to list[i] == target?
options: It stops with an error message
It says nothing at all

quiz.question: Arrange the tokens to build the body of searchName.

sections.title: Same Shape, New List of Words

chunks.text: searchCity(char list[][20], int size, char target[]) is the same shape pointed at cities[5][20]. The loop and the strcmp test are untouched.

check.question: What changes between searchName and searchCity?
options: The way two words get compared
The list handed in, and the name

chunks.text: With {"Carmen", "Tagbilaran", "Ubay", "Talibon", "Loon"}, searchCity(cities, 5, "Talibon") hands back 3.

check.question: Why does that call give 3?
options: Talibon is the third city listed
Talibon sits in row 3, counting from 0

chunks.text: Loop, strcmp, hand back i, and return -1; at the end. That shape never changes — not for numbers, not for words.

check.question: What has to be rewritten to search a new list?
options: Nothing about the loop itself
The compare test inside it

quiz.question: What two numbers print, and why?
options: 2 then 2, since both spellings reach the very same row
2 then -1, because strcmp treats U and u as different
3 then -1, since the rows are counted starting from 1
2 then 0, and the 0 means the second search failed
